question: Two electromagnetic waves A and B have wavelengths $10^{-10}\text{ m}$ and $10^{-6}\text{ m}$ respectively. Which wave has greater photon energy? Justify using the wavelength-energy relation.

options.A: Wave B has greater photon energy because it has the larger wavelength.
options.B: Both waves have the same photon energy because they are electromagnetic waves.
options.C: Photon energy is $E = \frac{hc}{\lambda}$, so it is inversely proportional to wavelength. Since wave A has the smaller wavelength, $10^{-10}\text{ m}$, wave A has greater photon energy.
options.D: Wave A has lower photon energy because its wavelength is shorter.
